subtopics.name: Geography
subtopics.summary: Location, borders, physical terrain, and major river systems of Kerala.

facts.title: Capital & Geographic Scope
facts.content: The capital is Thiruvananthapuram. Kerala covers a geographic area of 38,863 sq km across 14 administrative districts.

facts.title: Major Rivers & Drainage Systems
facts.content: Key river systems flowing through the region include: Periyar, Bharathappuzha (Nila), Pamba, Chaliyar.

facts.title: Geographical Landscape & Highlights
facts.content: Branded as 'God's Own Country'. Highest literacy rate and highest Human Development Index (HDI) in India. World-famous backwaters, spices, Ayurveda, and Kathakali.

subtopics.name: History & Culture
subtopics.summary: Historical formation, classical/folk dances, and vibrant festivals of Kerala.

facts.title: State Formation & Language
facts.content: Kerala was formally instituted on 1 November 1956. Official language(s): Malayalam (Classical Language).

facts.title: Dance Forms & Traditional Arts
facts.content: Celebrated traditional and folk dance forms: Kathakali, Mohiniyattam (2 Classical Dances), Theyyam, Koodiyattam.

facts.title: Major Festivals & Celebrations
facts.content: Prominent cultural festivals: Onam (Thiruvonam), Vishu, Thrissur Pooram.

subtopics.name: Government & Polity
subtopics.summary: Constitutional leadership, administrative structure, and state symbols of Kerala.

facts.title: Governor & Constitutional Head
facts.content: The current Governor is Arif Mohammed Khan.

facts.title: Chief Minister & Administration
facts.content: The Chief Minister of Kerala is Pinarayi Vijayan.

facts.title: High Court Jurisdiction
facts.content: Judicial jurisdiction falls under Kerala High Court (Kochi).

facts.title: Official State Symbols
facts.content: State Animal: Indian elephant | State Bird: Great hornbill | State Flower: Golden shower (Kanikkonna) | State Tree: Coconut palm.

subtopics.name: Economy & Agriculture
subtopics.summary: Natural resources, minerals, industrial clusters, and agriculture in Kerala.

facts.title: Mineral Wealth & Natural Resources
facts.content: Principal minerals and resources: Ilmenite, Monazite sands (Thorium rich), Zircon, Rutile (Chavara).

facts.title: Economic Profile & Industries
facts.content: Kerala plays a vital role in India's economy through key agricultural production, manufacturing corridors, and services.

subtopics.name: Places, Monuments & Tourism
subtopics.summary: Heritage landmarks, national parks, and tourism attractions in Kerala.

facts.title: Historic Monuments & Cultural Sites
facts.content: Prominent monuments and heritage landmarks: Padmanabhaswamy Temple (world's wealthiest temple), Bekal Fort, Mattancherry Dutch Palace, Hill Palace Kochi.

facts.title: National Parks & Protected Areas
facts.content: Key protected conservation areas: Silent Valley National Park, Eravikulam National Park (Nilgiri tahr habitat), Periyar National Park.

subtopics.name: State Schemes & Awards
subtopics.summary: Prominent welfare schemes, civic initiatives, and state honors of Kerala.

facts.title: Key State Welfare Schemes
facts.content: Notable welfare initiatives and government programs: K-FON (Kerala Fibre Optic Network), LIFE Mission, Karunya Arogya Suraksha Padhathi.
